extra.message: User input from the 'name' query parameter is directly interpolated into HTML via f-string without any escaping or sanitization. An attacker can inject arbitrary HTML/JavaScript by providing a name like '<script>alert(1)</script>'. This is a reflected XSS vulnerability.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: User-controlled content (containing the 'name' query parameter) is passed through Jinja2's Template().render() on line 41 after being interpolated into HTML via f-string on line 38. An attacker can inject Jinja2 template expressions like '{{7*7}}' which will be evaluated server-side. This Server-Side Template Injection can lead to remote code execution via Jinja2's access to Python object hierarchy (e.g., ''.__class__.__mro__[1].__subclasses__()'). The test file even has a TODO confirming this vector (lines 38-41 of tests/test_main.py).

The 'public_ip' value obtained from an external HTTP service response (line 36: public_ip_response.text) is directly interpolated into HTML without any escaping or sanitization. If the external service is compromised, returns malicious content, or is replaced via the PUBLIC_IP_SERVICE_URL environment variable, an attacker can inject arbitrary HTML/JavaScript.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: The application makes an HTTP GET request to a URL from the PUBLIC_IP_SERVICE_URL environment variable without any URL validation, allowlisting, or scheme restrictions. While the URL comes from an environment variable rather than direct user input, if an attacker can control this variable (e.g., through container misconfiguration, CI/CD compromise, or .env file manipulation), they can make the server send requests to arbitrary internal or external URLs, potentially accessing internal services or exfiltrating data.

The SUPER_SECRET_NAME is hardcoded as 'John Ripper' in source code instead of being loaded from an environment variable or secret manager. The FIXME comment on the same line acknowledges this should use os.getenv(). Hardcoded secrets in source code are exposed to anyone with read access to the repository and cannot be rotated without code changes.

The SUPER_SECRET_TOKEN is hardcoded as '5u93R53Cr3tT0k3n' in source code instead of being loaded from an environment variable or secret manager. The FIXME comment on the same line acknowledges this should use os.getenv(). Hardcoded tokens in source code are exposed to anyone with read access to the repository and cannot be rotated without code changes. This token appears to be an authentication/authorization credential.
